tasks.title: Make the pre-push hook executable in git and have doctor catch it
tasks.goal: The pre-push quality gate must actually run in every fresh clone or worktree. Today .githooks/pre-push is committed as mode 100644, so git ignores it with 'hook was ignored because it's not set as executable' and the author check, lint and tests are silently skipped.
criteria: .githooks/pre-push is committed with mode 100755 (git update-index --chmod=+x); git ls-files -s shows 100755
A test asserts the committed mode is 100755 and that the hook runs scripts/prepush.py
scripts/setup_dev.py makes sure the hook is executable when it sets core.hooksPath

scripts/doctor.py FAILs, with the fix for the user's OS, when core.hooksPath is set but the hook would not run: on macOS/Linux the file is not executable; on every OS git ls-files -s shows 100644 (Git for Windows often has core.fileMode=false, so do not rely on the file's own mode there); never a silent PASS
A real `git push` from a fresh clone runs the gate (no 'hook was ignored' hint) on macOS and Windows (Git Bash)
Full pytest suite, ruff and scan_secrets pass; core.hooksPath and --no-verify are never bypassed to get there

tasks.title: Pinned requirements.txt + run.sh (macOS) / run.bat (Windows), tested on both
tasks.goal: One command takes a fresh GitHub ZIP to a running app on macOS or Windows.
criteria: Every direct dependency pinned to an exact version; installs cleanly on Windows x64 and macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel wheels exist)

run.sh (started as `bash run.sh`): finds python3.12/python3.11/python3, creates .venv if missing, installs requirements via .venv/bin/python, stops with a clear message if .env is missing, launches the app

run.bat (started as `.\run.bat` from PowerShell or double-click/cmd): tries `py -3.12`, `py -3.11`, then `python`; uses .venv\Scripts\python.exe directly (no activation, no PowerShell scripts, so the downloaded-file execution policy can't block it); same .env check; launches the app; `pause` on error so the window doesn't vanish

First run with no .env: copies .env.example to .env, opens it in Notepad (Windows) or TextEdit via `open -e` (macOS), prints what to fill in, and exits; next run checks that placeholders were replaced (section 0.4.4)
Messages are written for non-coders (what happened, what to do next); run.bat ends with `pause` on any error so double-click users can read it; the URL is printed
Before launching, runs a quick connectivity check (scripts/check_endpoints.py) and warns in plain language if a class service can't be reached, without stopping the app
Both open the browser via the app (webbrowser / Gradio inbrowser), not OS commands
No ffmpeg or other system installs required
Tested from a fresh GitHub ZIP on one Windows and one Mac machine; results in the PR
Behavior matches PROJECT.md section 0.4 (Path 1) exactly; update section 0.4 and README Setup in the same PR if anything differs
requirements.txt contains no AI SDK or local-model package (check_models.py passes)
